title: Molecular communication
introduction: Development of experimental microfluidic systems using chemical reactions to produce and modify molecular signals and demonstrate paradigms in the field of molecular communication.

paragraphs: My work in molecular communication focuses on the creation of an experimental platform combining chemistry, microfluidics, instrumentation, electronics and signal processing to transmit signals encoded in molecules. This work was carried out during my contract in Yansha DENG's team, in the Department of Engineering at King's College London.

To design and build this molecular testbed, I designed and manufactured six syringe pumps by combining computer-aided design, 3D printing, electronic assembly and connection to an Arduino board, the development of an I²C communication protocol, and the development of control software using C++ and Python. The six syringe pumps are open source so that the wider scientific community can benefit from them.

I then demonstrated the effectiveness of my testbed by generating and transmitting signals encoded in chemical solutions over a distance of up to 25 metres, and successfully decoding the message at the receiver. The signals were also processed through chemical reactions to optimise their quality.

Alongside this experimental work, I applied my knowledge of artificial intelligence to develop a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) using Python, TensorFlow and scikit-learn to analyse UV-Visible spectroscopy measurements and decode complex molecular signals.

This work enabled me to publish a total of 2 scientific papers and also gave me the opportunity to lead the setup and organisation of an organic chemistry laboratory within the Department of Engineering, from purchasing equipment to implementing safety and quality-control protocols.
